## What the consolidation says

The two reports were strongly complementary: A gave the target architecture (separate run-group / node / edge / display / controller axes, a YAML↔Markdown parity matrix, a six-phase rollout), B gave the ground truth (a family is one OS process or a workspace-deferred child, plus the concrete traps: `release_workspace` has no PID predicate, slot admission and root listing share one predicate, failure never propagates through `%wait`, kill doesn't cascade to family members).

All held up, with one refinement: B's claim that family members "cannot be `%wait` targets" is really an autocomplete-visibility plus name-validation block — the runtime wait index actually indexes planner rows individually under `<base>--plan`, so member referenceability is *inconsistent* rather than absent, which itself strengthens the case for explicit dependency edges. 2. **Hoods vs. group metadata** — reconciled: hoods demonstrate the display-side UX, but authoritative execution membership must be explicit `group_id` metadata, never prefix-derived.
3. **Runtime strategy** — A's single compiled run-graph is the end state; B's incremental path (delegate control flow to YAML first, add an `if`-equivalent once the migrated corpus demands it) is the sequencing.

The report ends with seven merged questions, the load-bearing one being whether "family" keeps meaning *phases of one CL* or becomes *a group of peers* — every design axis wants opposite answers for the two.

import json
from sase.history.chat import load_chat_for_resume
history = load_chat_for_resume({{ resolve.path | tojson }})
injected_history = (
    "%xprompts_enabled:false\n"
    "# Previous Conversation\n\n"
    f"{history}\n\n"
    "---\n\n"
    "%xprompts_enabled:true\n"

import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_file=$(mktemp /tmp/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff)
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)
